📊 Mistral Large 4 isn't only a cybersecurity model. Here are its coding and agent numbers.

Most of the coverage of Mistral Large 4 ("Le Chonk") focuses on security, but the coding and knowledge-work results are worth a look too.

**Coding agents**
- 61.7% on DeepSWE v1.1
- 59.4% on SWE-Atlas-QnA
- 28.3% on Terminal-Bench 4
- 49.8% combined on the Coding Agent Index, ahead of DeepSeek V4 Pro 0813 and Qwen3.8 Max

**Knowledge work**
- 59.9% on AutomationBench (business workflows)
- 1,393 Elo on AA-Briefcase (long-horizon professional tasks)

**Overall**
As of Oct 29, it's the fifth-best open-weights model on the Artificial Analysis Intelligence Index. It also takes image input, so the same model can read screenshots, charts and documents alongside code.

**How to read these numbers**
Benchmarks are a starting point. The results come from the article and Mistral's reporting, and your own codebase and workflows are the real test. Open weights make that test easier to run, since you can evaluate on private data without sending it to a third-party API.

**What I'd try first**
- Point it at a real repo and compare its patches to your current model's
- Test it on your internal runbooks and business workflows
- Try the low, medium and high reasoning settings to see where the cost/quality tradeoff lands for your tasks (reasoning can't be fully disabled)

One licensing note: it's released under the Mistral Ecosystem Open-Weight License, an MIT derivative that limits model-as-a-service offerings. Check that it fits your use case.

Has anyone started comparing open-weight models on their own agentic workloads? I'd like to hear what you're seeing.

#AI #LLM #CodingAgents #OpenSource #SoftwareEngineering #MistralAI
